rundown: Chippewas beat Hornets 28-7 at Kelly/Shorts Stadium in Mount Pleasant, MI. Chippewas led 14-7 at the half and never looked back. The 1st quarter decided it: Chippewas won it 7-0. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 88%).
Scoring: Hornets 1 touchdown and 0 field goals; Chippewas 4 touchdowns and 0 field goals. The last score: B. Townsend run for 6 yds, for a TD (C. VanHuis KICK) (4th quarter, 1:05).

Leading the way — Hornets: Brian Salazar Jr. 13/28, 103 yds, 1 INT; Isaiah Ene 8 car, 67 yds, 1 TD; Onterrio Smith Jr. 4 rec, 47 yds. Chippewas: Jadyn Glasser 11/19, 105 yds; Nick Woodford 23 car, 119 yds; Nasir Williams 3 rec, 57 yds.
Where Chippewas won it: they outgained them 424 yards to 211 and held the ball 39:48 to 20:12.
Against the closing line (DraftKings): Chippewas closed as 17.5-point favorites and covered by 3.5; the total closed at 41.5 and they combined for 35, under by 6.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 11, 7:22 PM ET. It had Hornets 25% and Chippewas 75%, projecting Hornets 16.8 – Chippewas 27.1 (43.9 total, Chippewas by 10.4).

Final: Hornets 7 – Chippewas 28. Right winner: it had Chippewas at 75%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Hornets came in with a 42% below average attack and a 32% leakier than average defense (2-8, 17 scored and 29.3 allowed a game over 10 games), worth about 24 and 23 games of evidence. Projected to score 16.8, they scored 7 (−9.8 points, 58% under); projected to allow 27.1, they allowed 28 (+0.9 points, 3% over).

Chippewas came in with a 21% below average attack and a 18% leakier than average defense (4-5, 19.8 scored and 23.8 allowed a game over 9 games), worth about 174 and 171 games of evidence. Projected to score 27.1, they scored 28 (+0.9 points, 3% over); projected to allow 16.8, they allowed 7 (−9.8 points, 58% under).

The bigger miss was Hornets' scoring (-9.8 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 35 against 43.9 projected (-8.9), about the 28th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±15.5).

Margin: Chippewas by 21 against Chippewas by 10.4 projected, about the 76th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±15.3).

An ordinary result: inside the range the simulations expected most of the time.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Weather (45°F · ? mph wind): Chippewas ×0.94, Hornets ×0.94. Market (Line movement signal): Chippewas ×1.02, Hornets ×1.00. It favored Chippewas, who did beat their projection by more than the other side did.

review.title: Against the market
review.body:
CMU ML (-1200) at -1200: the algo gave it 88% vs 89% fair (-1.1 pts) — won (+0.1u); lost to the close (closing fair chance 88%). SAC ML (+750) at +750: the algo gave it 12% vs 11% fair (+1.1 pts), THE PICK — lost (-1u); beat the close (closing fair chance 12%). CMU -17.5 (-105) at -105: the algo gave it 47% vs 49% fair (-2 pts) — won (+1u); same number as the close. SAC +17.5 (-115) at -115: the algo gave it 53% vs 51% fair (+2 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. OVER 42.5 (-112) at -112: the algo gave it 51% vs 50% fair (+0.3 pts) — lost (-1u); lost to the closing 41.5 by 1. UNDER 42.5 (-108) at -108: the algo gave it 49% vs 50% fair (-0.3 pts) — won (+0.9u); beat the closing 41.5 by 1.

From the algo's snapshot to the close: total 42.5 → 41.5. The total moved away from the algo's number.

review.title: Where the public and the money were
review.body:
Splits (Action Network): spread: 49% of bets on Hornets, 47% of the money — Chippewas covered; total: 84% of bets on the over, 58% of the money — it went under; moneyline: 3% of bets on Hornets, 43% of the money.

The sharp side by the algo's read was Chippewas, who won and covered.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.778 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +9.1 points. It counts toward CFB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 65 graded CFB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.971 and gives home teams -1.5 points. Team corrections start after 3 graded games for a team.

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total within its normal range, margin within its normal range, the pick lost (-1u).
